PulseChain funding conversions and rebasing pool reserves
Finding and scope
A funded local conversion route is demonstrated. The e121 wallet bought pDAI with native PLS, issued
existing Synthetix sUSD, used inherited dHEDGE portfolios, withdrew sUSD and other synths, sold sUSD
through the existing Curve pool for pUSDT, and converted the pUSDT into native PLS. The legs are
observed transactions involving mixed inventory. They are not an isolated investment-profit calculation
or a fresh private-L2 funding proof.
Rebasing can materially change reserves in some inherited Curve pools. The PWRD and STBT pools
examined below use an implementation that prices from live ERC20 balances, less recorded admin fees.
Other pools handle balances differently, and the token itself may exclude the pool from rebasing. Current
yield availability must be established separately.
All investigation was read-only: public receipts, historical traces, logs, runtime code, storage and explicit
pure/view getters. No transaction, setter simulation, state override or signature was used. The source
pARB RPC remains unavailable.
Current pool and resource getters are pinned to PulseChain chain 369, block 27,691,754, hash 
0x37e17b339cdbdd71627ed1ed3da1cefc538790401685438094920b82ceac396a, 2026-10-02 04:47:55 UTC. The
additional destination-event census ends at block 27,692,266, hash 
0xaa2d9472094a89fce7f49279040ed6f831e108af14a8bba346ae6ebdf183087f. Historical receipts retain their own blocks
and hashes.
Follow the funding into actual market assets
The actor is 0x98c89980d1eae247ada3636ae27648f78e66e121. Exact pool-facing assets are pDAI 
0x6b175474e89094c44da98b954eedeac495271d0f, sUSD 0x57ab1ec28d129707052df4df418d58a2d46d5f51, and pUSDT 
0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7.
Owned native PLS
   │ observed market purchases
   ▼
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 234

Existing pDAI ── Synthetix DAI wrapper ── existing sUSD
                                             │
                     optional dHEDGE investment and mixed-asset withdrawal
                                             │
                                             ▼
                       Curve DAI/USDC/USDT/sUSD pool
                                             │ funded swap
                                             ▼
                               pUSDT received by e121
                                             │ subsequent market swaps
                                             ▼
                                Native PLS received by e121
Proposed new L2 issuance ── authenticated destination mint ──► existing sUSD
                              THIS ENTRY IS STILL UNPROVED
The September 7 purchase transaction supplied 10,101,010 PLS to the PulseX router and received 
48,483.983138861573080045 pDAI from two market paths. The subsequent wrapper mint deposited 
48,483.98 pDAI and issued 48,362.77005 sUSD after the 25-basis-point mint fee. This is an observed
local entry requiring owned input capital.
Across five September wrapper transactions, the prior Synthetix integration study (Appendix 69)
reconciles 136,554.715815649876218232 pDAI deposited to 136,213.329026110751527686
sUSD issued. At the current pin the wrapper cap is 20 million pDAI, and its pDAI balance is 
5,354,411.586932067826653098: approximately 14.6456 million pDAI below that cap. Other
checks and successful execution are still required; this is one capacity measurement.
The repeated deposit contracts are inherited dHEDGE portfolios, including 
0x907feb27f8cc5b003db7e62dfc2f9b01ce3fadd6 and 0xd076b9865feb49a43aa38c06b0432df6b6cbca9e. Receipt burns and
underlying transfers show that withdrawals return portfolio assets, including sETH or sBTC alongside
sUSD. The project's historical contract source explains mixed-asset withdrawals; its current repository
text is architectural context rather than proof of an exact deployed implementation match. The historical
traces and receipt transfers are the evidence for the observed actions.

pUSDT received:

the wallet. The four sale/exit transactions cost 7,528.349405514803925374 PLS in gas. Earlier
purchases, wrapper fees, portfolio deposits, other withdrawn assets and remaining claims must also
enter any profitability calculation. The original 10.101-million-PLS purchase does not account for all
assets later withdrawn or sold.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 235

The native exits route through several markets, including pUSDC, pDAI and Atropa transfers. That
supports the integrated-market interpretation. An intermediate purchase followed by immediate resale is
not retained peg-defence inventory. These particular transactions convert inventory back to PLS; they do
not establish a permanent $1 bid or the operator's motive.
The existing sUSD Curve pool is 0xa5407eae9ba41422680e2e00537571bcc53efbfd. Its current view quotes return 
2,318.024207 pUSDT for 1,000 sUSD, 23,083.972283 for 10,000, and 221,933.602676 for
100,000. These are local relative prices, not external dollars. Average proceeds decline with size.
Current quotes neither reproduce the September executions nor prove a complete profitable cycle.
Which rebases actually reach the trading reserves?
T wo independent questions govern the result: does the token change this pool's balance, and does the
pool use that balance when pricing and paying trades?

The PWRD/STBT clones point to 0x55aa9bf126bcabf0bdc17fa9e39ec9239e1ce7a9. Its PulseChain runtime matches
the Ethereum explorer's published deployed bytecode exactly. Its verified _balances() reads each token's 
balanceOf(pool) minus recorded admin_balances; pricing and liquidity calculations use that result. The
sampled getters reconcile those quantities. Curve's rebasing metapool source illustrates this
architecture. A positive rebase can increase LP-owned trading reserves, alter relative quotes and permit
arbitrage that redistributes counter-assets; a negative rebase can reduce those reserves. Neither
direction supplies external purchasing power by itself.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 236

Lybra's clones point to 0xa85461afc2deec01bda23b5cd267d51f765fba10, also an exact runtime match to the 
Ethereum published code. This is a two-asset CryptoSwap, rather than the rebasing StableSwap
metapool implementation. Its invariant and exchange calculations use stored balances. _claim_admin_fees()
includes a live-balance synchronization step. Establish which successful call reaches that step and how
quotes change around an actual rebase before budgeting this route as an automatic buffer.
The OUSD pool's matched destination implementation at 0x5f890841f657d90e081babdb532a05996af79fe6 stores
trading balances and reports live excess as admin balance. The current OUSD implementation is 
0x33db8d52d65f75e4cdda1b02463760c9561a2aa1. Its opt-in acts on msg.sender; a governance wallet calling it
opts in that wallet, not the Curve pool. Current Origin documentation describing remote governance opt-
in must not be imported into this older implementation. A token change or compatible new venue may
be necessary for different treatment.
UZD's verified token source permits removeRigidAddress(pool) only to DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. Removing the
exclusion is a distinct permission from operating a rebalancer. Pool recognition still needs testing after
any change. No such action was performed here.
Reserve eUSD and mUSD expand or contract through issuance/redemption. FRAX AMOs and DOLA Feds
manage permitted supply. Those mechanisms should remain separate from holder-balance rebases,
static receipt exchange-rate growth and ordinary swaps.
Rebasing capacity is not current income
PWRD's verified token calculates holder balances from a factor derived from controller-reported assets.
STBT's verified implementation permits issuer-authorized positive or negative interest distributions, with
interval and ratio limits. These are specific supply mechanisms, not proof of common group ownership or
newly generated underlying income.
STBT's lastDistributeTime remains 2023-05-10 09:01:11 UTC. This recorded state does not support
assuming current continuous treasury-interest accrual on the fork.
Lybra's code makes the funding leg particularly clear: excessIncomeDistribution receives eUSD, directs the
fee portion to its service-fee pool, burns excess payer shares and transfers surplus stETH to the payer.
Reducing shares redistributes claims to remaining eUSD holders. The stETH input must exceed recorded
deposits; it is not created by the distribution itself.
At the pin, Lybra holds 2,964.739596779408217723 stETH against 2,964.739596779408217375
recorded deposits: only 348 wei of excess. Its last-report timestamp is 2024-09-06 08:13:35 UTC. This
branch currently supplies no material surplus stETH to that distribution route. The fee ledger and
accumulated fees also require accounting. This does not rule out future local staking or a different
funded strategy; it identifies the resource that must change.
There are two useful rebase designs. An eligible treasury account can receive genuine net yield, sell the
incremental inventory and use the proceeds to support cheap pDAI. Alternatively, a compatible pool can
recognize balance growth directly, allowing prices and arbitrage to redistribute liquidity. The latter
benefits the relevant LP claims; count only the system-owned share, and do not count the same yield
again as a separate treasury asset. Positive rebase supply can also pressure the rebasing coin's price,
and losses can shrink support capacity.
Highest-value next evidence
The added query of the configured Synthetix destination bridge covers blocks 27,683,121–27,692,266,
with zero query errors and no FinalizeSynthTransfer or InitiateSynthTransfer events. This extends the prior
observation; it does not prove that every possible alternative bridge or issuance method is inactive.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 237

The most valuable next piece for the fresh L2 funding thesis is one successful, independently
reproducible PulseChain transaction that follows:
New accepted source commitment/message
 → configured messenger 0x25ace71c97b33cc4729cf772ae268934f7ab5fa1
 → correct cross-domain sender 0x136b1ec699c62b0606854056f02dc7bb80482d63
 → bridge 0x39ea01a0298c315d149a490e34b59dbf2ec7e48f.finalizeSynthTransfer
 → authorized Issuer mint into the existing sUSD identity
 → funded conversion and inventory reconciliation
This is the configured copied Optimism/Synthetix path. Control of copied Arbitrum administration or a
separate optimistic arbitration module does not substitute for its messenger and counterpart
authentication. A proposed pARB entry requires its own proved gateway or an authorized, compatible
adapter/configuration change.
The source commitment must be fresh, rather than reuse an inherited pre-fork withdrawal. Preserve the
accepted root/message proof, sender authentication, mint receipt, exact pool token, recipient, market
proceeds and source liabilities. The private RPC need not become public to observe a destination
settlement, but inaccessible source accounting can leave backing unresolved.
This priority follows three passes: the first found successful local issuance; the second established actual
market conversion and native proceeds; the third matched rebasing pool code and checked current
resource availability. More integration names would add less than proving the missing replenishment
entry. For the multi-year earnings branch, the next proof is separately an actual resource-backed
distribution that increases owned, realizable net assets and reconciles the pool's balances and quotes.
The strengthened thesis is therefore: existing local issuance can feed funded market
conversions; compatible rebasing assets can redistribute genuine yield into treasury or LP
inventory; fresh authenticated issuance or realized net earnings must establish
replenishment at the required scale. These results establish useful local connections without
establishing external-dollar parity or indefinite financing.
Reproduction
Bulk evidence is in ignored artifacts/pulsechain-funding-and-rebases-20261002/; earlier mint receipts remain in
artifacts/pulsechain-synthetix-integrations-20261001/. Explicit manifests are under Research/experiments/
pulsechain_funding_*_20261002.json, pulsechain_rebase_resources_20261002.json and 
pulsechain_fresh_synth_delivery_20261002.json. The event retry covers all four timed-out pUSDT incoming
ranges and returned no additional events or query errors. Getter failures and the unavailable debug
tracer are preserved; successful historical tracing used trace_transaction.
Run the offline reconciliation into a new output path:
python Research/scripts/analyze_pulsechain_funding_and_rebases.py \
  --root artifacts/pulsechain-funding-and-rebases-20261002 \
  --prior artifacts/pulsechain-synthetix-integrations-20261001 \
  --output /tmp/pulsechain-funding-reproduction.json
The generated report preserves input hashes, fixed snapshots, reconciled asset flows, matched
implementations, current quotes and explicit limits. The verifier checks receipts, transaction actors,
chronology, burned portfolio receipts, identical amounts sold and spent, native trace payouts, runtime
identity, balance accounting, resource state and destination-event coverage. Research verification does
not require executing blockchain actions.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 238
